criteria.title: Functional scope: sync, sharing, offline, history

levels.0: Treats it as 'upload and download files', with no mention of multiple devices, offline edits or sharing.
levels.1: Covers multi-device sync, sharing and resumable uploads, but never pins down offline duration, version history, or that co-editing inside a file is out of scope.
levels.2: Covers sync of create/edit/rename/move/delete, shared folders with roles, resumable 10 GB transfers, days-long offline, 30-day history and restore, on-demand mobile/web, and explicitly rules out real-time co-editing.

criteria.title: Non-functional targets and the no-lost-edit invariant

levels.0: No durability, propagation or correctness targets.
levels.1: States 10 s propagation and high availability, but treats 'never lose an edit' as a generic durability line rather than a conflict-handling requirement.
levels.2: States the invariant (an acknowledged version is never lost; no version is overwritten without telling the user), 10 s p99 propagation, metadata availability above block availability, and bandwidth efficiency as a goal.

levels.0: No storage numbers, or a total with no derivation.
levels.1: Gets 200 PB logical, but never separates metadata from bytes or never sizes the shard count.
levels.2: 200 PB logical, dedup and erasure coding to about 450 PB raw; about 170 TB of metadata (file rows, journal, block index) giving 128 shards; and concludes shard count is set by storage, not throughput.

levels.1: Derives commits per second but misses either upload bandwidth or the concurrent-connection count.
levels.2: 400M commits/day = 4,630/s (13,900 at 3× peak), about 9,260 downloads and listings/s, 18.5 Gbps upload average, 15M open connections giving 450 gateways and 90 API instances sized for losing one of three zones.

levels.0: A single 'upload file' endpoint that carries the bytes through the API.
levels.1: Separates block upload from commit, but the commit has no parent revision or idempotency key, or change listing has no cursor.
levels.2: /blocks/check returning presigned URLs for missing hashes, a commit with parent_rev and an idempotency key returning 409 on conflict, cursor-paged GET /changes, and a data-free doorbell channel.

levels.0: One 'files' table with a blob column, or no shard key.
levels.1: Separates metadata from blocks, but shards by user or file so a commit spans shards, or has no ordered journal.
levels.2: Shards metadata by namespace so a commit is one local transaction (journal append, file row, head increment), keeps a gap-free per-namespace journal, a separate block index sharded by hash, and justifies relational shards over a wide-column store.

criteria.title: Metadata plane, block plane and notification path

levels.0: Bytes flow through the API servers; no notification path.
levels.1: Draws presigned uploads and a metadata service, but change events are a dual write or the notification path is missing.
levels.2: Walks upload (hash, check, direct PUT, conditional commit), propagation (CDC or outbox to a topic, notifier, gateways or APNs/FCM, listing from cursor) and download, with a time budget for the 10 s target and shards replicated across zones.

criteria.title: Chunking, block size and dedup scope

levels.0: Uploads whole files, or splits without hashing.
levels.1: Uses fixed blocks keyed by hash, but cannot say why fixed blocks fail on insertions or what block size trades off.
levels.2: Compares whole-file, fixed 4 MiB and content-defined chunking, quantifies the index cost of smaller blocks, and treats cross-user dedup as a privacy side channel with a mitigation.

criteria.title: Sync protocol: cursor, three trees, Merkle hashes

levels.0: Compares full folder listings on every sync.
levels.1: Uses a journal and cursor, but the client cannot distinguish a local delete from a remote add.
levels.2: Journal plus cursor for O(changes) catch-up, a remote, local and synced tree on the client, and Merkle directory hashes placed where they belong: convergence checks and recovery when a cursor is unusable.

levels.1: Detects conflicts but resolves them with locks or an automatic merge that cannot work for binary files.
levels.2: Optimistic parent_rev check at commit, conflicted copy for the loser, edit-beats-delete, stable file ids so moves do not resurrect paths, and why version vectors are unnecessary with a per-namespace serialiser.

levels.1: Uses WebSockets, but pushes full change data so a lost or duplicate message corrupts state, or ignores mobile.
levels.2: WebSocket or long poll on desktop, APNs/FCM on mobile, doorbell-only messages so correctness lives in the cursor, per-device coalescing, and jittered reconnects answered from the head cache.

levels.1: Covers instance and shard failover, but not the reconnect storm, GC racing a commit, or what breaks first at 10×.
levels.2: Gives a zone-loss timeline (sockets drop, replicas promoted, idempotent retries, jittered reconnect), GC with a grace period longer than history, mass-delete recovery, and at 10× names gateways and hot shared namespaces first, then directory-based resharding and a home region per namespace.

levels.1: Generic trade-offs (consistency vs availability) not tied to this design.
levels.2: Each key choice (planes split, 4 MiB fixed blocks, presigned transfers, namespace sharding, journal and cursor, conflicted copies, doorbells) with the alternative and the specific reason it lost.
